statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $0.4(x + 15) = 0.25x + 9$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied only the $x$ by 0.4 and left the 15 alone, so I solved $0.4x + 15 = 0.25x + 9$, which gave $0.15x = -6$ and $x = -40$.
I got to $0.15x = 3$ but slipped a decimal place and divided 3 by 1.5, which gave 2.
I moved the 6 to the right side by adding it instead of subtracting it, so I got $0.15x = 15$ and $x = 100$.

hints: Distribute the 0.4 to both terms inside the parentheses.
After distributing, collect the $x$-terms on one side and the constants on the other. Multiplying everything by 100 removes the decimals if you prefer.

solutions.elegant: Multiply both sides by $20$ to clear the decimals: $8(x + 15) = 5x + 180$, so $8x + 120 = 5x + 180$, $3x = 60$ and $x = 20$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
